title: Four fleet registers disagreed on which vehicles Human Services leased

beats.text: Four City registers counted the same Human Services fleet differently.

visual.sub: Four registers gave different answers about the City fleet

beats.text: Two lists agreed on 96 vehicles but differed on 11 identification numbers.
Central Shops leased the vehicles to the department.

visual.kicker: The City’s own leasing operation may have billed for two extra vehicles

beats.text: Two extra vehicles could mean up to $2,988 a year.

visual.kicker: The City’s own leasing operation may have billed for two extra vehicles

beats.text: The department said some vehicles on a later list had already been returned.

visual.kicker: The City’s own leasing operation may have billed for two extra vehicles

beats.text: Auditors also found 28 vehicles below a proposed mileage benchmark.

visual.kicker: Mileage and route estimates depended on what staff were doing

beats.text: The agency said work with tools and emergency responses also mattered.

visual.kicker: Mileage and route estimates depended on what staff were doing

beats.text: Those annual records have no vehicle identification numbers.

visual.kicker: The City reported actual lease spending without vehicle-level detail

beats.text: In June 2014 four fleet controls remained open.

visual.kicker: Four fleet controls were still open after two years

beats.text: The published record gives no amount for a lease credit.
